hero.description: Eight world titles and an entire country accelerating together. The asphalt holds the technique, bravery, and history of icons who transitioned the sport and transformed Sunday mornings into the golden era of our motorsport.

preF1.title: The Entrepreneur
preF1.text: Before Europe, Emerson and his brother Wilson founded a workshop in São Paulo, building go-karts and the iconic 'Fitti-Porsche'. Split between running a business and racing, the pressure was suffocating: motorsport was expensive, and he had to succeed in England almost instantly, as their local entrepreneurship financed his single, risky shot.

lotus72.title: The World's Youngest
lotus72.text: Driving the legendary black and gold Lotus 72D, Emerson stunned the planet by capturing his first world title. At just 25 years old, he became the youngest world champion in F1 history at the time (a record that stood for 33 years), officially launching Brazil's dynasty at the top of the podium.

mclaren74.title: Consolidating a Champion
mclaren74.text: Displaying his strategic side, Emerson shocked the grid by leaving Lotus for the rising McLaren team. Behind the wheel of the classic M23, he faced one of the most balanced and tense seasons in history against Ferrari. This second championship proved his genius didn't rely on a single team, but on a brilliant mind.

copersucar.title: The Brutal Dream
copersucar.text: At his peak, Emerson left McLaren to pursue his most daring endeavor with Wilson: Copersucar-Fittipaldi, the only Brazilian team in F1 history. This romantic dream collapsed under mechanical failures, a lack of budget against European giants, and merciless, cruel criticism from the local media and public, who never forgave the lack of immediate wins.

indy.title: Rebirth in America
indy.text: When many declared his career over after the toll of the Copersucar years, Emerson crossed the Atlantic to conquer IndyCar. Two victories at the legendary Indianapolis 500 and the 1989 championship cemented Emmo as a timeless global icon.

preF1.title: The Beginning and the Grit
preF1.text: To race karts, Nelson had to hide his passion from his father, a former minister. Without financial support early on, he traveled to Europe where he worked as a mechanic, sweeping workshop floors to fund his dream and developing the mechanical intelligence that would become his trademark.

brabham81.title: The First Crown at Brabham
brabham81.text: Adopted by Bernie Ecclestone at Brabham, Piquet became the team's technical leader. In 1981, overcoming the infernal heat of Las Vegas and extreme physical exhaustion, he pushed the BT49C to the limit to beat the favorites and claim his first world title.

brabham83.title: The Turbo Era and the Victory Theme
brabham83.text: Developing the brutal BMW Turbo engines alongside designer Gordon Murray, Nelson shaped the legendary Brabham BT52 and became the first F1 world champion of the turbo era. It was also in this year, at the Brazilian GP, that the iconic 'Victory Theme' played for the first time on TV: an idea by broadcaster Galvão Bueno to immortalize Brazilian triumphs, debuting exactly with a Piquet victory.

williams87.title: Cold War and the Overtake of the Century
williams87.text: At Williams, he lived an epic internal battle with Nigel Mansell. It was in this car, in 1986, that he immortalized the maneuver of the century in Hungary: overtaking Ayrton Senna around the outside, drifting sideways. In 1987, he used his surgical setup precision to win the psychological war against his own team and become a Three-time Champion.

benetton.title: The Last Brilliance
benetton.text: Considered a veteran by many, Nelson went to Benetton to prove his genius was intact. He pulled rabbits out of a hat with memorable victories on extremely demanding tracks like Suzuka and Adelaide, ending his brilliant Formula 1 journey at a high level.

posF1.title: Endurance and Survival
posF1.text: After F1, Nelson survived a horrific crash at the Indy 500 that severely crushed his legs. Defying doctors, he returned to racing in Endurance events with the iconic McLaren F1 GTR at Le Mans. Today, he remains a living legend of global motorsport.
